profile.name: Peace Khutso Molimo
profile.title: BSc Computer Science Honours Candidate
profile.tagline: Designing intelligent systems for equitable, efficient public service delivery in South Africa.
profile.bio_intro: I am a BSc Computer Science Honours candidate at the University of the Western Cape, with a background in Physical Sciences. My research sits at the intersection of machine learning and public service delivery — exploring how intelligent systems can solve real, everyday problems faced by South African citizens.
profile.bio_detail: My Honours research focuses on developing a Smart Queue Management System for high-traffic government service centres such as the Department of Home Affairs and SASSA. The system integrates an online booking platform with machine learning models — including K-Nearest Neighbours, Random Forest, and Neural Networks — to predict waiting times and improve operational efficiency. This work is driven by a commitment to fairness, accessibility, and data ethics, particularly in contexts where algorithmic bias can have real consequences for vulnerable communities.

research.title: Smart Queue Management System
research.subtitle: Reducing waiting times in South African public service centres through machine learning
research.abstract: South African public service centres are widely associated with long queues, with citizens often waiting more than five hours — sometimes leaving without being assisted. This research proposes a Smart Queue Management System integrating online booking with ML algorithms to predict waiting and service times using queue length, staff availability, customer category, and arrival time.

terms.label: Term 1
terms.summary: Literature review, problem framing, and initial research proposal covering predictive coding frameworks and system architecture.

documents.title: Literature Review: Queue Management Systems & ML Approaches
documents.description: A comprehensive survey of existing queue management systems, examining traditional M/M/s models versus ML-based approaches. Reviews Random Forest, KNN, and Neural Network applications in service-time prediction.

documents.title: Research Proposal: Smart Queue Management System
documents.description: Formal research proposal outlining the development of an ML-powered queue management platform for South African public service centres, including POPIA compliance strategy and cybersecurity considerations.

documents.title: Progress Report: Term 1 Supervisor Meeting Notes
documents.description: Annotated meeting minutes covering dataset selection strategy, model benchmarking methodology, and revised milestones. Includes discussion of the digital divide challenge for walk-in versus pre-booked users.
